Estimate bias across multiple facet pairs

Source: R/api-bias-collection.R, R/api-plotting-bias-collection.R
estimate_all_bias.Rd

Estimate bias across multiple facet pairs

Usage

estimate_all_bias(
  fit,
  diagnostics = NULL,
  pairs = NULL,
  include_person = FALSE,
  drop_empty = TRUE,
  keep_errors = TRUE,
  max_abs = 10,
  omit_extreme = TRUE,
  max_iter = 4,
  tol = 0.001
)

# S3 method for class 'mfrm_bias_collection'
summary(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'mfrm_bias_collection'
print(x, digits = 3, ...)

# S3 method for class 'summary.mfrm_bias_collection'
print(x, digits = 3, ...)

# S3 method for class 'mfrm_bias_collection'
plot(
  x,
  pair = NULL,
  type = c("overview", "scatter", "ranked", "heatmap", "abs_t_hist", "facet_profile"),
  draw = TRUE,
  preset = "standard",
  ...
)

Arguments

fit

Output from fit_mfrm().

diagnostics

Optional output from diagnose_mfrm(). When NULL, diagnostics are computed with residual_pca = "none". Must match this fitted analysis; see mfrmr_compatibility_layer for migration of saved diagnostics.

pairs

Optional list of facet specifications. Each element should be a character vector of length 2 or more, for example list(c("Rater", "Criterion"), c("Task", "Criterion")). Explicit specifications may include canonical "Person" regardless of include_person. When NULL, all 2-way combinations of modeled facets are used. Each combination may appear only once, regardless of facet order.

include_person

If TRUE and pairs = NULL, include "Person" in the automatically generated pair set. "Person" denotes the source column supplied as person to fit_mfrm() and remains opt-in because these cells condition on fitted JML person measures or MML EAP scores.

drop_empty

If TRUE, omit empty bias tables from by_pair while still recording them in the summary table.

keep_errors

If TRUE, also retain per-pair error rows in the returned errors table. Either way, errors remain in summary$Error and do not stop the batch.

max_abs

Passed to estimate_bias().

omit_extreme

Passed to estimate_bias().

max_iter

Passed to estimate_bias().

tol

Passed to estimate_bias().

object

A result from estimate_all_bias().

...

For plot(): With pair, additional arguments to plot.mfrm_bias(), such as top_n or sort_by. The overview rejects additional arguments.

For summary(): Reserved; additional arguments are rejected.

x

A result from estimate_all_bias().

digits

Number of significant digits used for printing; calculations and returned tables retain their precision.

pair

An exact Interaction label from summary(x)$overview, or its row number. NULL (default) shows all requested pairs.

type

"overview" shows signed cell estimates grouped by pair. With pair supplied, the default becomes "heatmap"; "scatter", "ranked", "abs_t_hist" and "facet_profile" select the corresponding plot.mfrm_bias() view.

draw

Draw the figure. FALSE returns its data without opening a device.

preset

A package plot preset, for example "standard" or "monochrome".

Value

A named list with class mfrm_bias_collection.

For summary(): summary() returns a summary.mfrm_bias_collection list: overview has one row per requested interaction, cells combines retained cell tables with an Interaction identifier and explicit PointAvailable, ScreenAvailable and ScreenPositive fields, errors lists failed pairs, and optimization_failures retains cell-level optimizer records. Original cell columns, including facet levels, observed counts, signed Bias Size, conditional S.E., t and any GPCM profile status, are preserved. settings, fit_identity and notes retain provenance and interpretation. Print methods return their input invisibly.

For plot(): Invisibly, a ggplot object carrying its saved plot payload for plot_data(). For the overview, plot_data() provides table (all combined cells, including unavailable rows), overview, errors, optimization_failures, fit_identity, settings, axis labels and notes. as_ggplot() returns the overview ggplot. A selected pair returns the ordinary bias ggplot with collection_pair and fit_identity provenance added to plot_data().

Details

This function orchestrates repeated calls to estimate_bias() across multiple facet pairs and returns a consolidated bundle.

Bias/interaction in MFRM refers to a systematic departure from the additive model for a specific combination of facet elements (e.g., a particular rater is unexpectedly severe on a particular criterion). See estimate_bias() for the mathematical formulation.

When pairs = NULL, the function builds all 2-way combinations of modelled facets automatically. For a model with facets Rater, Criterion, and Task, this yields Rater\(\times\)Criterion, Rater\(\times\)Task, and Criterion\(\times\)Task. With include_person = TRUE, Person\(\times\)facet pairs are prepended in the fit's facet order. They are conditional plug-in likelihood screens, not jointly fitted Person\(\times\)facet terms. A single warning records this boundary for the batch.

The summary table aggregates results across pairs:

  • Rows: number of interaction cells estimated

  • Points: cells with an available bias estimate (including bounded optima; inspect BiasStatus in the combined cells)

  • ScreenAvailable, ScreenUnavailable: cells with/without a usable conditional screening statistic

  • ScreenPositive: count of available cells with \(|t| \ge 2\); NA when no screening statistic is available, including failed pairs

  • Significant: backward-compatible alias for ScreenPositive

  • MeanAbsBias: average absolute available bias magnitude (native ability units)

  • Status: available, partial, unavailable, empty, or failed; available refers to conditional screening, not formal inference

  • FormalInferenceEligible / PrimaryReportingEligible: always FALSE; these conditional plug-in interaction statistics are screening evidence

Per-pair failures (e.g., insufficient data for a sparse pair) are captured in errors rather than stopping the entire batch. There is no collection-wide multiplicity correction. Cells and pairs reuse the same observations and fitted calibration. Adjusting their screening tail areas would not establish formal family-wise error or false-discovery control. A screen-positive result is a prompt for review, not proof of unfairness; no screen-positive cells does not establish absence of interaction. Search-boundary points remain visible, with missing screening statistics and the ScreenStatus/ScreenReason returned by estimate_bias().

summary() method: Summarize all retained bias screens

For summary(): No model, diagnostics or cell calculation is repeated. The overview counts finite bias estimates from successful cell optimizations separately from cells with a finite screening statistic and positive finite conditional SE. ScreenPositive is missing when no statistic can be screened, rather than reporting zero. Failed pairs remain visible even when the original batch used keep_errors = FALSE. Older collections without retained tables are labeled not_retained; they are not recalculated.

A positive bias shift increases expected coded scores conditional on the fitted model. It does not necessarily mean better performance or unfair leniency. Baseline calibration and Person uncertainty are held fixed. Different pairs use overlapping data, so do not add their observed counts to obtain a study sample size. The overview's mean absolute bias describes magnitude only; use the signed cell estimates to study direction. Counts cover retained estimate_bias() cells: unobserved combinations and cells omitted by the chosen screening options are not reconstructed. No multiplicity-adjusted confirmatory decisions are supplied.

plot() method: Explore bias across facet pairs

For plot(): The overview plots every finite retained bias estimate, without ranking or a significance cutoff. Positive shifts increase expected coded scores under the fitted model; score meaning depends on the rubric. Vertical spreading only separates cells visually and has no statistical meaning.

Filled circles have a usable conditional screening statistic; open circles retain a point without one. These symbols indicate availability, not whether a cell is flagged. Pair labels report usable statistics / retained cells and the range of observed row counts per cell (n), not independent Person counts. Pairs share observations. Empty, failed and unavailable pairs remain labeled, without substituting a point at zero. The vertical zero line means no conditional shift, not a threshold for practical importance.

No model or diagnostics are recalculated. The overview supplies no intervals, multiplicity correction or formal bias test. Review the individual cell counts, optimizer status and subject-matter explanations; selecting a pair after this overview does not make its subsequent analysis confirmatory. Titles and interpretation notes are returned outside the figure.

Output

The returned object is a bundle-like list with class mfrm_bias_collection and components such as:

  • summary: one row per requested interaction

  • by_pair: named list of successful estimate_bias() outputs

  • errors: per-pair error log

  • settings: resolved execution settings

  • primary: first successful bias bundle, useful for downstream helpers

Typical workflow

  1. Fit with fit_mfrm() and diagnose with diagnose_mfrm(). For RSM / PCM reporting runs, prefer method = "MML" plus diagnostic_mode = "both" in the diagnostics call.

  2. Run estimate_all_bias() to compute the requested multi-pair interactions.

  3. Inspect summary(bias_all)$overview for availability and magnitude, then summary(bias_all)$cells for all retained cells and their observed counts. Use plot.mfrm_bias_collection() for the overview or a named pair.

  4. Use report <- mfrm_report(bias_all) to retain the full search, failed pairs and all cells in one report; export_summary_appendix() saves its tables. Supply study_context to state rubric endpoints and score direction. The by_pair list also feeds reporting_checklist() or facet_quality_dashboard().

  5. For a substantively justified joint interaction model, use facet_interactions in fit_mfrm() and compare_mfrm() on compatible fits. Selecting terms from these screens makes same-data comparisons exploratory; it does not create a prespecified confirmatory test.

Saved-result reuse

The returned fit_identity records the fitted analysis for reuse with reports and exports. Recreate older results from the saved fit and matching diagnostics using the original screening options; no model refit is needed. See mfrmr_compatibility_layer for migration instructions.

Session plot defaults

See mfrmr_visual_diagnostics for options(mfrmr.plot_preset), argument precedence, and appearance when saving or reusing a plot.

See also

estimate_bias(), mfrm_report(), compare_mfrm(), reporting_checklist(), facet_quality_dashboard()

Examples

# Long-running workflow; run explicitly when needed.
# example("estimate_all_bias", run.dontrun = TRUE)
if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
toy <- load_mfrmr_data("example_core")
fit <- fit_mfrm(toy, "Person", c("Rater", "Criterion"), "Score",
                method = "MML")
diag <- diagnose_mfrm(fit, residual_pca = "none", diagnostic_mode = "both")
bias_all <- estimate_all_bias(fit, diagnostics = diag)
summary(bias_all)
head(summary(bias_all)$cells)
report <- mfrm_report(bias_all, study_context = c(
  score_direction = "Higher coded scores indicate better performance"))
report$tables$overview
head(report$tables$bias_cells)
} # }
# Long-running workflow; run explicitly when needed.
# example("summary.mfrm_bias_collection", run.dontrun = TRUE)
if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
ratings <- load_mfrmr_data("example_bias")
fit <- fit_mfrm(ratings, "Person", c("Rater", "Criterion"), "Score",
                method = "MML")
screens <- estimate_all_bias(fit)
review <- summary(screens)
review$overview
head(review$cells[, c("Interaction", "Bias Size", "ObsN", "ScreenAvailable")])
} # }
# Long-running workflow; run explicitly when needed.
# example("plot.mfrm_bias_collection", run.dontrun = TRUE)
if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
ratings <- load_mfrmr_data("example_bias")
fit <- fit_mfrm(ratings, "Person", c("Rater", "Criterion"), "Score",
                method = "MML")
screens <- estimate_all_bias(fit)
p <- plot(screens)
plot_data(p, "overview")
plot(screens, pair = "Rater x Criterion", type = "ranked")
} # }
